run: A2: SMOL as a second held-out domain. Inconclusive, the pool saturates.

condition_2_strong_model_below_ceiling.note: For comparison LaBSE scores 0.6928 on the xSIM++ pool, which is why that one can separate models and this one cannot.

why_it_saturates: The distractors come from the xSIM++ FLORES pool, a different corpus from SMOL. A model can rule them out on domain alone without understanding the sentence, so the gold is effectively unopposed. xSIM++ works because each distractor is its own gold with one token changed.
conclusion: This does not replicate the Phase B base-model finding and should not be reported as if it did. The ordering matches (LaBSE fine-tuned > v1 released > LaBSE > e5-base), but the two arms are separated by 14 queries out of 2,462, and v1 beats LaBSE here while losing to it on the xSIM++ pool, so the two pools are not measuring the same thing.
caveats: Both exit conditions were written in Phase A. Only the lexical one was checked before this pool was built and evaluated. That is the error this file records.
A pool that would work needs distractors from SMOL itself, near neighbours of each gold, mined with a model that is not in the comparison. That is untested.
The xSIM++ perturbation code is not released, only the generated FLORES files, so the published method cannot be applied to SMOL.
